name: Navigation and Resource Timing
plain: Reports DNS, connect, TLS and download timings for the page and each resource.
meaning: Reveals connection speed and CDN behavior, whether a request hit the cache, protocol (h2, h3) and TLS reuse. Cross-origin detail needs the Timing-Allow-Origin header, otherwise sizes and phases are zeroed.

data.metric: One entry per resource, about 20 timestamps each

fields.name: transferSize
fields.precision: exact for same origin or TAO; 0 if cached

limits.headline: Can see how fast the page and each file loaded for you
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens as the page loads
can: Get timings for DNS, connection, security setup and download
Learn your connection speed and if a file came from cache
Learn the web protocol used, such as h2 or h3
Get full detail for outside files only if their site allows it
cannot: See what is inside other sites' files
Know who you are by itself
See full outside detail without that site's approval

story.what_it_is: Browsers report timings for the page and each file it loads: DNS, connection, security handshake and download.

marketing.name: Navigation timing
marketing.pitch: Describes how pages can read detailed timings about how they loaded.

marketing.name: Resource timing
marketing.pitch: Describes how pages can measure the timing of each file they request.

story.for_you: You never see it. Sites quietly collect how fast each page and image loaded for you. Your slow connection is turned into data that helps them fix slow pages.
story.for_makers: It is the base of web speed monitoring. Teams compare load times by country, network and device. It also lets ad and tracker scripts see timing of other files, so browsers limit cross site detail.

use_cases.example: A monitoring service collects load times from real visitors and shows a map of the slowest regions.
A retailer finds that its image server is slow in one country and adds a closer cache.
A video site checks how long the first video segment takes to arrive and adjusts quality.
A game portal measures asset download times to see how long players wait before playing.
An ad network measures how long each ad takes to load and drops slow ad partners.
A fraud tool compares timing with the claimed location. A login that says Paris but loads like Asia looks odd.
A news site measures third party script times to learn which tags slow the page.

technical_bounds: Buffer limited to 250 resource entries by default

value.legit_uses: Real user monitoring, Core Web Vitals
value.abuse: Infer cache state, ISP speed, VPN latency

history.change: Resource timing gets responseStatus and contentType
